chapter: Cab Calloway's band, features and small groups
title: Illinois Jacquet, "Rhythm Cocktail" and Cab keeping control of soloists
summary: Jacquet demanded a feature and got "Rhythm Cocktail", a version of "Flying Home"; Jones thinks Cab limited solos so he would not lose control as Duke did.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And here comes Illinois Jacquet. Here comes the wrecking crew starting in now. He's had gentlemen in the band all the time had been pretty good. Now they get Illinois Jacquet. Well, "Flying Home" Illinois - this thing. Everybody owns it. Hamp says it's his. Arnett Cobb says it's his, Illinois says it's his. So he comes in the band. So now you've got to make "Flying Home" for him. But Jacquet comes in arguing. "I've got to have something to play, Cab." "I ain't going to sit there like that, like Shad and Jonah and them other guys that don't play nothing. I've got to have something to play." You know. So they made him a number -- Buster made an arrangement, called, "Rhythm Cocktail," which is only "Flying Home," you know, with the same solo they used. You know, same thing. So he goes on with this for about six, seven, eight months. Finally Cab said, "Rhythm Cocktail," is out. Jacquet said, "Oh, no. That's it. I'm giving him my notice. That's it. That's it. 'Rhythm Cocktail' is out, I give my notice in." So they went

in the room and talked and everything, and then finally they come out, and "Rhythm Cocktail" was back again. But no sooner than he got a chance, you know, they found somebody, you know, like Sam Taylor, Quebec, you know, Ike, out he went. He wouldn't let you hold no stick over his head, you know. I think that was mostly the reason why the guys didn't play much, like Johnny with Duke and Lawrence Brown and them, because he didn't want that to get out of hand to where he wasn't in control. I think he felt like Duke wasn't in control of the thing, you know, with Ben and them.
At the mercy of the guys.

Yeah. You know, like a guy wanted to take a solo, and then everybody was going to be asking for them, you know. And that was a drag for him, you know. He was the big -- this is Cab, Cab Calloway, you know. Sure. So he made it when he had less talented musicians, you know. But he liked to have good ones around him all the time. He liked to brag you about the band, you know. He liked the people to brag about it, you know.
